era: in the new era's tech (shouting across fields)

speaker: mother
text: Your mother, shouting across three fields: all this food and you're still so thin!
notes: From the sample run. Shown on the first Farming life.

speaker: farmer
text: A farmer found an old mammoth drawing. He's sure it's a planting guide.
notes: From the sample run: it works, nobody knows why.

speaker: priest
text: The rock guy's temple is enormous now. The priests want it bigger.
notes: The tutorial guy's shrine grows every era.

speaker: cousin
text: The fire's out. Your cousin says the old way takes too long.
notes: The Stone Age keystone as an answer.

speaker: naysayer
text: I'm the old Naysayer's nephew. He was far too positive. Farming? Dirt?
right effects: Priests -10; Village +5; set kept_naysayer; clear naysayer_banished
notes: The worse Naysayer you earned by banishing the first.

speaker: farmer
text: The ground is too hard to plant. Your cousin is attacking it with his hands.

speaker: cousin
text: Your cousin dug half a row with a pointed stick and fell asleep in it.

speaker: farmer
text: Your cousin sharpened his stick on a rock. Now he wants to sharpen everything.
epitaph: Invented sharp tools, and new ways to lose a finger.

speaker: farmer
text: A wild ox keeps eating your crops. It seems to like you.

speaker: naysayer
text: Staying in one place? What if the food moves?

speaker: farmer
text: The grain sacks are too heavy to carry to the barn.

speaker: ox
text: The ox followed you home. It's standing in the house, chewing.
epitaph: Invented the tame ox. It was already tame. You just asked.

speaker: farmer
text: Your neighbour swears you have fewer sheep than yesterday. Neither of you can prove it.

speaker: priest
text: The priests say the rain stopped because you're counting things.

speaker: naysayer
text: Counting? You'll never run out of numbers, so what's the point?

speaker: priest
text: Someone scratched marks to track the grain. The priests want to know what they mean.
epitaph: Invented counting, and with it, the tax collector.

id: # Leanings: the wheel (its breakthrough kills you and still counts)

speaker: neighbours
text: The village over has something round they keep rolling around. Everyone's looking at you.
notes: From the sample run. Refusing counts toward the pottery ending, later.

speaker: cousin
text: Your cousin made a wheel, but square. It doesn't roll away. He considers this a win.
notes: Feeds the square wheel bad idea.

speaker: narrator
text: You carved something round. It's sitting at the top of a hill. It wants to go.

id: # The plough (keystone: needs sharp tools and the tame ox from earlier lives)

speaker: priest
text: Your furrows are crooked. The priests say crooked rows anger the Gods.

speaker: farmer
text: What if the ox dragged the sharp stick, and we just walked behind it?
right effects: use sharp-tools; use tame-ox; Harvest +20; Village +10
epitaph: Invented the plough. The ox did most of it.

speaker: kid
text: A kid wove a hat out of grain. The birds are following him.
notes: Feeds the grain hat bad idea.

speaker: neighbours
text: The neighbours built a fence. It's on your side of the stream.

speaker: neighbours
text: The village over is having a harvest feast. You're not invited, but you can hear it.

speaker: priest
text: No rain for weeks. The priests want a sacrifice. They're looking at the ox.

speaker: mother
text: You're always in that field. When do I get grandchildren?

speaker: mother
text: You planted all this and you still look like a scarecrow. Did you eat?

speaker: farmer
text: Everyone has a sharp stick now. Arguments are going very differently.

speaker: ox
text: The ox wants the good corner of the house.

speaker: priest
text: Now that you can count, the priests want a tenth of everything.

speaker: farmer
text: The plough works so well that nobody has to farm all day. Now they're bored.

id: # Fame: high-stakes cards once you've invented something this life

speaker: neighbours
text: The village over copied your invention and is selling it back to you.

speaker: priest
text: The priests say your invention is a miracle, and miracles belong to the temple.

speaker: farmer
text: Farmers from three valleys came to see your invention. They brought their goats.

speaker: priest
text: Now that you're famous, the tax collector has questions.

speaker: narrator
text: A quiet day in the fields. The crops grow. Nobody looks at you.
